source.note: Product source is private. These are reviewed implementation references at the pinned mainline; substring checks guard drift and do not establish runtime acceptance.

claims.claim: Each Slack thread and MCP task gets an isolated EC2 worker and persistent encrypted EBS workspace.

evidence.contains: Every Slack thread, and every task a developer hands over from an AI tool, gets its own isolated, persistent workspace.

claims.claim: Idle compute stops while workspace files and conversation state remain available for resume.

evidence.contains: idle reaper stops compute while preserving workspace files and conversation state.

claims.claim: Slack and MCP task tools for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can start or continue tasks.
There is no published AgentX release or npm package; source-checkout installation requires locally built release assets and user-pushed images.

evidence.contains: No AgentX release is published yet
container images you have pushed yourself

claims.claim: FSL-1.1-ALv2 is source-available, not OSI open source, and each release converts to Apache 2.0 two years after it ships.

evidence.contains: release becomes Apache 2.0 two years after it ships

claims.claim: Historical selected Pro batch: 40 of 50 tasks resolved according to saved graders, with all 50 outcomes inspectable. This is not an official full-benchmark score or a model comparison.

claims.claim: New and resumed coding sessions install the runtime verification extension. It reports missing checks and gives one additional attempt on regression.
Worker task results store checks.json and can carry a compact check report.

Publication reruns readiness checks, reports checks when requested, and preserves the older refusal path. CodeBuild evidence runs before the PR sink; it does not block publication on failing gate results.
